title: Victor Wembanyama's Game 3 Hopes Clouded By Concussion Protocol Despite Optimism - NewsBreak
text:
By Reign Amurao ,
1 hours ago The San Antonio Spurs had a great start to the postseason, thanks to Victor Wembanyama’s strong outing in Game 1 on Sunday. Wembanyama had 35 points to lead the Spurs to a 111-98 win and have a 1-0 start. However, the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year suffered an unfortunate injury in Game 2 that led to the team losing to the Portland Trail Blazers.
Wembanyama left Game 2 in the second quarter after he fell and hit his head on the floor. He was ruled out by the Spurs and was put in the league’s concussion protocol. Before Game 3, his situation is still uncertain since he still has to fulfill a few prerequisites before the NBA and the organization would let him to play.
ESPN’s Shams Charania gave an update on Victor Wembanyama on Wednesday’s episode of “NBA Today.”
“I’m told Victor Wembanyama did report to the Spurs facility this morning, and his status is uncertain for Game 3,” Charania said. “I am told that Victor Wembanyama is hopeful to travel with the team on Thursday to Portland, but he and the team won’t know for sure until then. Right now, he’s in the concussion protocol, and that means he cannot participate in unrestricted activities for at least 48 hours. So that would be Thursday night.”
Charania said that Wembanyama could start with some “light work starting tonight if his symptoms don’t worsen.” The two-time All-Star will need time to rest and recover, and the ESPN reporter said that the Spurs will take it day-by-day.
Keldon Johnson is Not Worried About Playing Without Victor Wembanyama There is concern for the Spurs’ playoff hopes after Victor Wembanyama suffered the injury. However, the 2026 Sixth Man of the Year, Keldon Johnson , is not worried about it. According to him, they have what it takes to hold the fort without their best player. Johnson said that they are a “battle-tested” group and know what adjustments they have to make in Game 3.
The Spurs had a tough 106-103 defeat in Game 2 against the Blazers, but the team kept it close. Luke Kornet played in Wembanyama’s place and had a productive night. He finished with 10 points, nine rebounds and two steals.
Ahead of Game 3, the Spurs will need to work well together without Wembanyama.
